gold: Brown tumor secondary to primary hyperparathyroidism due to parathyroid carcinoma

selector.rationale: The presence of a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger with histopathology showing fibrous tissue, woven bone, and giant cells with multiple osteoclast-like nuclei is most consistent with Brown Tumor, which is a known complication of Primary Hyperparathyroidism and Osteitis Fibrosa Cystica.

rejected.label: Primary Hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of primary hyperparathyroidism, the current presentation is more consistent with a complication of this condition rather than the condition itself.
